SI-4: Heterogeneity of morphometric similarity networks in health and schizophrenia

DC-1.detail: The study combined 11 datasets. Six are present in the provided list: Cam-CAN (camcan), IXI (ixi), NKI (rockland), OASIS-3 (oasis3), Utrecht (clinical_baseline healthy controls), and GROUP (clinical_baseline healthy controls). The remaining five (AOMIC [id1000, piop1, piop2], DLBS/dibs, Narratives, and SALD) are categorized as MULTI-SITE (N>=2) as they are not specifically listed.
DC-1.supporting_text: We included healthy participants from ten publicly available datasets: the Amsterdam Open MRI Collection (aomic) (id1000, piop1 and piop2) datasets 14 , the Cambridge Centre for Ageing and Neuroscience (camcan) dataset 15 , the Dallas Longitudinal Brain Study (dlbs) dataset 16 , the Information eXtraction from Images (ixi) dataset (http://braindevelopment.org/ixidataset/), the Narratives (narratives) dataset 17 , the Open Access Series of Imaging Studies (oasis3) dataset 18 , the NKI-Rockland (rockland) dataset 19 and the Southwest University adult lifespan (sald) dataset 20 . One dataset is not publicly available and consisted of a large longitudinal sample of individuals with schizophrenia and healthy participants aged 16-68 years (at baseline) from the Utrecht Schizophrenia project and the Genetic Risk and Outcome of Psychosis (GROUP) consortium.

answer.Utrecht: normative training (20% of healthy controls) and testing (80% of healthy controls and all schizophrenia patients)

answer.GROUP: normative training (20% of healthy controls) and testing (80% of healthy controls and all schizophrenia patients)

answer.MULTI-SITE (N>=2): includes AOMIC, DLBS, Narratives, and SALD; used for normative training (90%) and testing (10%)

DC-2.detail: Ten cross-sectional datasets were split into training (90%) and test (10%) sets. The clinical dataset (Utrecht/GROUP) was split such that 20% of healthy controls went to training and 80% of healthy controls plus all schizophrenia patients went to testing.
DC-2.supporting_text: For normative modeling, each of the ten datasets containing only healthy controls was split into a training set ( ≈ 90%) and a test set ( ≈ 10%) ... For the clinical dataset, all individuals with schizophrenia, as well as 80% of the healthy controls, were included in the test set, while the remaining healthy controls (20%) were included in the training set.
DC-2.location: Janssen2024.pdf.md: MATERIALS AND METHODS / Normative modeling of morphometric similarity

DC-3.detail: The training set included 4310 healthy participants. The total healthy control (HC) sample size across all 11 datasets is 5002 (calculated as 4310 train + 692 test HC). Note: The total test set of 859 includes 167 schizophrenia patients and 692 HC.
DC-3.supporting_text: The training set included 4310 participants and the test set 859 participants. ... The per-dataset splits were created ... preserving the distribution of age, sex, and scanner ... All individuals with schizophrenia were included in the test set.
DC-3.location: Janssen2024.pdf.md: MATERIALS AND METHODS / Normative modeling of morphometric similarity; Fig. 1

DC-4.detail: Weighted mean and pooled SD were calculated using healthy control data from the 11 sites. Mean age for HC: 41.33 years; SD: 21.45. Training phase values are not reported separately but the split was stratified to preserve age distribution. Minimum age is 16 (from Utrecht/GROUP). Maximum age is inferred as ~90 from OASIS-3/Cam-CAN distributions.
DC-4.reason: Global mean and SD for healthy controls were not explicitly stated but calculated using site-specific N, mean, and SD provided in Fig 1 and Table 1A (using only HC data for the clinical site). Weighted mean = sum(N*mean)/sum(N). Pooled SD = sqrt([sum((N-1)sd^2) + sum(N(mean-global_mean)^2)]/(sum(N)-1)). Max age is inferred from Fig 1's age distributions.

DC-5.detail: Gender counts were calculated by weighting the percentages provided for each dataset (using only HC data for the clinical site). Overall HC: 58.0% female (N=2903/5002). Train phase (N=4310) values are inferred based on the stratified split reported in the paper.
DC-5.reason: Global gender counts for healthy controls were not explicitly stated but calculated using site-specific N and %Female provided in Fig 1 and Table 1A (using only HC data for the clinical site). Female N = sum(N*%F). Train phase counts are inferred using the global percentage (58.0%) applied to the train N (4310).
